title: Deadlock
provenance: DXMT changelog v0.73 (github.com/3Shain/dxmt/releases). playX18 (highball-db#243, 2026-09-28): rated 4, playable with minor issues, Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0, DXMT, a full standard match played; engine and Highball version not stated. Hetens (highball-db#387, 2026-10-08): rated 4 after 19 minutes, Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.3, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r19, DXMT, "temperatures on the higher side but still very good".
notes: DXMT's changelog lists the MetalFX temporal scaler output as fixed. A report has a full standard match playable on DXMT on an M5 Pro, with two costs: about ten minutes of shader compilation before the game stops stuttering, and audio crackle, which that player fixed by setting the Mac's output to 88.2 kHz in Audio MIDI Setup. A second M5 Pro report (19 minutes on DXMT) says it runs very well and only runs warm.

anticheat.note: anti-cheat present; Linux/Proton support does not extend to macOS — userspace path works for some titles

knownIssues.symptom: Audio crackles (reported in the main hub on an M5 MacBook Air, highball#187, and in matches on an M5 Pro, highball-db#243).
knownIssues.cause: Most likely the same as Counter-Strike 2's, another Source 2 game: it keeps very little sound queued and at 48 kHz the Mac asked Wine for more at a time than it had (measured on Counter-Strike 2, highball#127). Not measured on Deadlock itself
knownIssues.fix: Highball 0.10.3 and later carry the fix that cured Counter-Strike 2's crackle (default engine r19 and later, Wine 11 engine r14 and later), not yet confirmed on Deadlock (highball#187). On older engines, setting the Mac's output to 88.2 kHz in Audio MIDI Setup worked for one player

knownIssues.symptom: Stutter for the first minutes of a match (reported on an M5 Pro, DXMT).
knownIssues.fix: none needed, it settles after about ten minutes.
